INDIVIDUAL SPECIES GUIDE · NOT A STOCK LISTING

Sun Conure

The Sun Conure is a vivid, medium-small South American parrot with yellow, orange and green plumage. It is often highly social and energetic, but its piercing calls and need for engagement deserve serious thought before choosing one.

Scientific nameAratinga solstitialis
Typical adult sizeAbout 30 cm long; approximately 100–130 g, with individual variation.
Lifetime planningOften around 20–30 years in captivity; estimates and individual outcomes vary.

Overview and appearance

Sun Conures are known for bright yellow and orange plumage, green wing feathers and a long tapered tail. Young birds can show more green, with colour developing as they mature. They are native to northern South America and are active, social parrots rather than quiet cage birds.

Their brilliant colouring can draw attention, but suitability depends on ordinary daily realities: noise, interaction, exercise and long-term care. Provide safe opportunities to climb, investigate and forage, and allow the bird to retreat from activity when it chooses.

Temperament and social needs

Sun Conures are frequently described as playful and people-oriented, yet each bird differs in confidence, affection and tolerance for handling. A social parrot still needs boundaries and independent activities. Interaction should follow the bird’s body language instead of assuming it wants to be held whenever someone is available.

They may make frequent contact calls, especially when excited or responding to household sounds. A predictable routine can help organise attention and quiet time, but does not eliminate calls. Families should teach children calm behaviour and maintain close adult supervision.

Typical adult size

An adult Sun Conure is about 30 cm long and often weighs roughly 100–130 g. Measurements vary between individuals. Use an enclosure with safe bar spacing and enough room to climb and move, with supervised exercise in a parrot-proof area each day.

Expected lifespan and long-term care

A Sun Conure can be a companion for around 20–30 years, though published figures vary and do not predict any particular bird’s life. Consider future care, housing and a backup guardian, rather than thinking of a small parrot as a short-term pet.

Talking and vocalisation

The Sun Conure is well known for a loud, high-pitched call that may be challenging in close housing. Individual vocal patterns vary, but it should not be selected on an expectation of quiet. Talking may occur, though speech is not the defining trait and is never guaranteed.

Intelligence and reward-based training

Curiosity makes positive-reinforcement training useful. Teach practical skills such as target following, stepping to a perch and entering a carrier, then offer simple puzzles and food-search activities. Frequent short sessions are more effective than long demands. Avoid responding with punishment to normal parrot calls.

Diet and nutrition

A balanced diet includes suitable formulated food and a range of fresh vegetables, with fruit and seed treats kept in perspective. Do not use an all-seed menu as a shortcut. An avian veterinarian can advise on an individual bird’s existing food, weight and any gradual changes; supplements should only be used with professional advice.

Housing, exercise and enrichment

Provide climbing space, safe perches, chewable enrichment and daily supervised activity outside the enclosure. Rotate toys, check them for wear and use foraging to make part of the day engaging. Make windows, fans, doors, plants and other household hazards safe before allowing exploration.

Suitability and questions before enquiry

This species may suit an active household that can accept a loud voice and offer regular social time, training and enrichment. It is not a fit for someone who needs a quiet companion or cannot supervise a busy bird. Consider close neighbours and the bird’s needs when everyone is away.

Ask about the individual’s age, diet, routine, noise patterns and handling preferences. Prepare safe exercise space and consider care over decades. Confirm current individual availability directly; the presence of this educational profile does not mean a Sun Conure is available.
